content:
Psoriasis is more than just a skin condition. The itching, dryness, redness, and flaking can affect confidence, sleep, and daily life. While conventional treatments often focus on temporary symptom relief, Ayurveda approaches psoriasis by correcting the internal imbalance causing the problem.

In Ayurveda, psoriasis is linked to imbalances in Vata and Kapha doshas, along with toxin accumulation in the blood and tissues. Instead of only treating the visible patches, Ayurvedic treatment focuses on cleansing the body, improving digestion, balancing doshas, and supporting long-term skin health naturally.

At Praanavaidya, psoriasis care is personalized based on your body constitution, lifestyle, digestion, and severity of symptoms.

What Is Psoriasis?

Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune skin condition where skin cells multiply faster than normal. This leads to thick, scaly, itchy patches that may appear on:

  • Elbows
  • Knees
  • Scalp
  • Lower back
  • Hands and feet

Common Symptoms

  • Red patches with silvery scales
  • Dry or cracked skin
  • Itching or burning sensation
  • Thickened nails
  • Skin irritation and inflammation

Symptoms often worsen due to stress, poor diet, lack of sleep, or seasonal changes.

Psoriasis in Ayurveda

Ayurveda relates psoriasis to conditions like Kitibha Kushta and Ekakushtha, which are types of chronic skin disorders.

Root Cause According to Ayurveda

Psoriasis develops when:

  • Digestion becomes weak (low Agni)
  • Toxins (Ama) accumulate in the body
  • Vata and Kapha become imbalanced
  • Blood tissue (Rakta Dhatu) gets affected

This imbalance eventually appears on the skin in the form of dryness, scaling, itching, and inflammation.

Ayurvedic Treatment for Psoriasis

Ayurvedic treatment for psoriasis focuses on internal healing and long-term balance.

1. Detoxification (Shodhana Chikitsa)

Detox therapies help remove toxins from the body and purify the blood.

Common Panchakarma Therapies

Virechana (Therapeutic Purgation)
 Helps cleanse excess Pitta and toxins from the liver and digestive tract.

Takradhara
 A calming therapy where medicated buttermilk is poured over the forehead to reduce stress and inflammation.

Abhyanga (Oil Massage)
 Improves circulation, nourishes dry skin, and calms Vata imbalance.

Basti (Medicated Enema)
 Supports detoxification and balances Vata, especially in chronic cases.

2. Diet for Psoriasis

Food plays an important role in skin healing. Ayurveda recommends a clean, simple, and anti-inflammatory diet.

Foods to Include

  • Warm freshly cooked meals
  • Leafy vegetables
  • Bitter vegetables
  • Seasonal fruits
  • Plenty of water

Foods to Avoid

  • Fried and processed foods
  • Excess dairy
  • Fermented foods
  • Sugary snacks and soft drinks
  • Excess spicy and oily foods

3. Lifestyle Recommendations

Simple lifestyle changes help prevent flare-ups:

  • Sleep on time
  • Reduce stress
  • Avoid smoking and alcohol
  • Practice yoga and meditation
  • Avoid excessive exposure to harsh chemicals

Yoga & Stress Management for Psoriasis

Stress is one of the biggest triggers for psoriasis flare-ups. Ayurveda combines physical and mental wellness practices for holistic healing.

Helpful Practices

  • Deep breathing exercises
  • Meditation
  • Gentle yoga stretches
  • Morning walks
  • Relaxation techniques

Managing stress helps calm inflammation and supports healthy skin regeneration.

Can Ayurveda Cure Psoriasis Permanently?

Psoriasis is considered a chronic condition, but Ayurveda aims to:

  • Reduce flare-ups
  • Improve skin healing
  • Lower inflammation naturally
  • Strengthen immunity
  • Improve quality of life

With proper treatment, diet, and lifestyle discipline, many people experience long-term relief.

Conclusion

Psoriasis can affect not only the skin but also emotional well-being and confidence. Ayurveda offers a holistic path that focuses on restoring balance from within rather than only managing surface symptoms. Through detoxification, mindful eating, stress management, and personalised therapies, Ayurvedic treatment aims to reduce flare-ups, calm inflammation, and support healthier skin naturally.

Yes. Stress is one of the most common triggers for psoriasis flare-ups.

Absolutely. Diet plays a major role in reducing inflammation and supporting skin
